questions.prompt: Identify the primary active transporter located on the basolateral membrane of renal tubular cells and describe its stoichiometry and role in establishing the cellular environment.
questions.modelAnswer: The Na-K-ATPase (sodium-potassium pump) utilizes ATP hydrolysis to extrude 3 Na^+ ions and take up 2 K^+ ions, maintaining a low intracellular [Na^+], a high intracellular [K^+], and a negative membrane potential (~ -70 mV) which provides the electrochemical driving force for most other tubular transport processes.

questions.prompt: Explain the mechanism and physiological purpose of the Na-H exchanger (NHE3) in the apical membrane of the proximal convoluted tubule.
questions.modelAnswer: NHE3 (Na-H exchanger) is a secondary active transporter that uses the inward Na^+ gradient to extrude H^+ into the lumen in exchange for Na^+ entry; this process is essential for reabsorbing ~80% of filtered bicarbonate (HCO_3^-) and facilitating bulk Na^+ reabsorption.

questions.prompt: Which specific transporter in the thick ascending limb (TAL) is the target of loop diuretics, and what is its ion stoichiometry?
questions.modelAnswer: The target is the NKCC2 (Na-K-2Cl cotransporter), which moves 1 Na^+, 1 K^+, and 2 Cl^- ions into the cell from the lumen using secondary active transport powered by the basolateral Na-K-ATPase.

questions.prompt: Describe the two primary pathways (transcellular and paracellular) for chloride reabsorption in the late proximal tubule.
questions.modelAnswer: Chloride is reabsorbed paracellularly down a concentration gradient (established by upstream water reabsorption) and transcellularly via apical Cl^-anion exchangers (e.g., SLC26A6) that exchange Cl^- for bases like formate or oxalate, followed by basolateral exit via Cl^- channels or K/Cl cotransporters.

questions.prompt: Identify the apical membrane transporter responsible for NaCl reabsorption in the early distal tubule and name the class of diuretics that specifically inhibits it.
questions.modelAnswer: The transporter is the NCC (Na/Cl cotransporter), which is an electroneutral symporter specifically inhibited by thiazide diuretics (e.g., chlorothiazide).

questions.prompt: Explain the two-step process of potassium secretion in the principal cells of the collecting duct.
questions.modelAnswer: Secretion involves basolateral K^+ uptake via the Na-K-ATPase to establish a high intracellular concentration, followed by passive K^+ exit across the apical membrane into the lumen through ROMK and BK channels, driven by the electrochemical gradient.

questions.prompt: Identify the specific water channel regulated by Arginine Vasopressin (AVP) and its cellular location in the absence of the hormone.
questions.modelAnswer: The channel is Aquaporin-2 (AQP2); in the absence of AVP, it is sequestered within intracellular vesicles called aggregophores just beneath the apical membrane.

questions.prompt: Describe the genomic mechanism by which aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption in the principal cells of the cortical collecting duct.
questions.modelAnswer: Aldosterone binds cytoplasmic mineralocorticoid receptors (MRs), translocates to the nucleus, and induces transcription of aldosterone-induced proteins (AIPs) that increase the number and open probability of apical ENaC channels and the activity/synthesis of basolateral Na-K-ATPase pumps.

questions.prompt: Identify the cell type and the primary active transporter responsible for hydrogen ion secretion in the late distal tubule and collecting duct.
questions.modelAnswer: α-Intercalated cells (Type A) utilize the H-ATPase (proton pump) and H-K-ATPase on their apical membrane to secrete H^+ ions into the lumen, often against steep concentration gradients.

questions.prompt: Explain the physiological characteristics that allow the thick ascending limb (TAL) to function as the "diluting segment" of the nephron.
questions.modelAnswer: The TAL is the diluting segment because it actively reabsorbs solutes (Na^+, K^+, Cl^- via NKCC2) while remaining virtually impermeable to water, thereby decreasing the osmolality of the tubular fluid to ~100 mOsm/L relative to the surrounding interstitium.
